claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five minutes the Council Procedures Bylaw (Bylaw 18155, s.38(1), consolidation of 2025-10-29) provides to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which about seventy people (60 to 80 entries on the committee's list) had been approved to speak on item 7.6 (IS03688, Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration Program Update). I used the brief's normalization unchanged. The body is the Infrastructure Committee, not City Council.
claims.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY ROW: Supported. (a) Standing limit is 5 minutes under s.38(1): 'Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes'. I got this wording from search-index extracts of the C18155 consolidation and of Bylaw 20226, which replaced s.38. I could not extract the text myself (see limitations). (b) Under item 1.4 the committee carried a motion moved by M. Janz to 'adjust the rules on time limits as set out in section 38 of Bylaw 18155 - Council Procedures Bylaw for the August 26, 2026, Infrastructure Committee meeting, so that: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes; and each member of Council has three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion.' Vote: In Favour (6) E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack, A. Paquette; Carried (6 to 0). (c) N = 64, inside the 60-80 band. QUALIFICATION 1, TWO-THIRDS (reviewer's calculation): the header lists 6 members present: Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz, Knack (Mayor, a member under s.15(3) of Bylaw 18156) and Paquette. 6 of 6 voted in favour. Two-thirds of all 6 members is 4, so 6 >= 4 and the vote met the special-resolution threshold in s.2/s.4 as the minutes record it. The motion also set Council members' limits: 3 minutes to ask questions and 3 minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. QUALIFICATION 2, COVERAGE: the wording covers 'each approved speaker' at the whole meeting, not only item 7.6 and not only one class of speaker. QUALIFICATION 3, ORDER: the motion is the third motion under item 1.4 (Adoption of Agenda), after agenda adoption and the Orders of the Day change. It comes before the item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion, before the item 2.4 motion making 7.6 the first item of business, and before the first public speaker on 7.6. QUALIFICATION 4, N, Requests to Speak for 7.6 (item 2.3, moved by A. Salvador, Carried 6-0), entries per panel: P1 15, P2 15, P3 15, P4 15, P5 4. N = 15+15+15+15+4 = 64. Entries with an organization: P1 2 (Edmonton Bike Coalition; YEG Bike Coalition), P2 8 (Bike Bus Alberta; Holyrood Voice; Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group; YEG Bike Coalition; Paths for People; Ward Métis Bikes x3), P3 3 (Let's Bike There YEG; Bike Edmonton; YEG Bike Coalition), P4 2 (Paths for People; YEG Bike Coalition), P5 0. Total 15. No additional-speaker motion for 7.6; the only additional-speaker motion (moved by E. Rutherford, Carried 4-0) was for item 7.4. QUALIFICATION 5, N-ALL by item: 7.1 5 entries (5 with an organization: Edmonton Construction Association x3, Big Lake Community League, PCL Construction Management Inc.); 7.3 1 (Alberta Avenue Business Association); 7.4 8 + 1 additional = 9 (6 with an organization: Alberta Ecotrust Foundation x2, Solar Alberta x2, Big Lake Community League, BILD Edmonton Metro); 7.6 64. N-all = 5+1+9+64 = 79 (reviewer's sum). Names are withheld, so a person approved on two items could appear twice in N-all and I cannot detect that. QUALIFICATION 6, N-SPOKE, presentation lists under 7.6: P1 16, P2 16, P3 18, P4 2. N-spoke = 16+16+18+2 = 52 (reviewer's sum). Entries with an organization: P1 5 (YEG Bike Coalition x2; Holyrood Voice; Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group; Paths for People), P2 6 (Bike Bus Alberta; Ward Métis Bikes x2; Let's Bike There YEG; Bike Edmonton; Paths for People), P3 1 (YEG Bike Coalition), P4 0. Total 12. The presentation panels do not match the Requests to Speak panels. Organizations that were approved in RTS Panel 2 appear in presentation Panel 1, for example. N and N-spoke are reported side by side only. QUALIFICATION 7: the carried minutes record no speaker given more or less than the limit and no motion extending any speaker's time. Five speaker attachments are listed under 7.6 (attachments 11-15: Panel 3 x2, Panel 2, Panel 1, Panel 4). QUALIFICATION 8: no City record stating a reason identified; the minutes record none. Searched: carried minutes and agenda; web search for the motion wording and for news of the 3-minute limit; the CBC report as republished on Yahoo; the Taproot agenda preview of 2026-08-24. All as of 2026-10-02. QUALIFICATION 9: none identified, but eScribe minutes returned HTTP 403 to my tool. A web search for the 3-minute motion wording across 2026 Edmonton minutes found no instance. This absence is weakly bounded. ALTERNATIVE ROWS: N=64 with the 50-90 band: Supported. N-all=79 with the 60-80 band: Supported; with 50-90: Supported. N-spoke=52 with the 60-80 band: Partially supported, because the queue-count element fails (52 < 60) while the 5-to-3 cut for every approved speaker is established. N-spoke=52 with 50-90: Supported. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive: if the holder's '70 in the current cue' is read as the people who actually presented on 7.6, the primary-band count fails. The story should say so beside the verdict.

limitations: Bylaw 18155 (essential source): my fetch tool retrieved the City's PDF at https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/Bylaws/C18155.pdf (about 413 KB). It could not decompress the text streams, and later retries returned HTTP 502. The s.38(1), s.2 and s.4 wording I rely on comes from search-engine extracts of that PDF and of Bylaw 20226, not from my own reading of the text. I could not read s.1, s.3(c) or the consolidation's list of amendments, so I cannot confirm that no amendment after 2025-10-29 bears on s.38. If the editor treats this as an inaccessible essential source, the methodology says this run should stop rather than count as a finding.

The search-index extracts disagree on s.38(6), the Councillor's time to speak to or close debate on a motion. Bylaw 20226 is reported as 2 minutes, while one extract of the City-hosted consolidation reads 5. So I cannot say whether the motion's 3-minute limit for members speaking to a motion was a cut or an increase. This does not affect the per-speaker limit.

Live minutes and agenda pages returned HTTP 403. I relied on the carried text (6 of 32 minutes items; 1 of 30 agenda items) and cannot say whether the live page carries any later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6. The carried text shows none.

In the carried item 7.6 text, the presentation list for Panel 4 has only 2 entries and runs straight into a motion, and there is no Panel 5 presentation list. This may be the complete record, or the list may be truncated in the carried text. N-spoke = 52 depends on it.
Bylaw 20226's date of passage could not be confirmed.

Qualification 9 is weakly bounded. eScribe minutes for meetings since 2025-10-29 returned HTTP 403 (for example, the 2026-04-27 City Council Public Hearing). I found no earlier s.38 time-limit adjustment by web search, but that is not evidence that none exists.
Names in the carried text are withheld, so I cannot count distinct persons. Duplicates in N-all, and any approved speaker who also appears in N-spoke, cannot be matched.
The CBC report and a search summary named members of the public who spoke. I did not reproduce those names.
unknowns: Whether the live post-meeting minutes carry any correction after approval.
Whether any amendment to Bylaw 18155 after 2025-10-29 changed s.38 before 2026-08-26.
Why the motion was moved. The minutes record no reason, and none was identified elsewhere.
Whether the Panel 4 presentation list in the carried text is complete.
Whether other Council or committee meetings since 2025-10-29 adjusted s.38 limits.

claims.suggested_one_line: Yes. The Infrastructure Committee voted 6-0 to cut each approved speaker from the bylaw's five minutes to three for the whole 2026-08-26 meeting. It had approved 64 people to speak on the bike-lane item (79 across the meeting), and 52 were recorded as presenting.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported, under the brief's primary count. At the start of the 2026-08-26 meeting (item 1.4), Infrastructure Committee member M. Janz moved to adjust the Council Procedures Bylaw's section 38 time limits for that day. Under the motion, every approved speaker on every item had a maximum of three minutes instead of the bylaw's standing five. Council members got three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to debate a motion. All six committee members voted for it, which meets the two-thirds special-resolution threshold. The committee's speaker list had 64 entries on the bike-lane item and 79 across all four items. Only 52 entries are recorded as having presented on the bike-lane item, so if the commenter's '70 in the queue' meant the people who spoke, the figure falls outside the 60-80 band. The finding is definition-sensitive. The minutes do not say why the motion was moved, whether speakers were complainants or where they came from, or which way anyone argued.
suggested_tldr: Standing limit under Bylaw 18155 s.38(1): five minutes per approved speaker.
Committee motion under item 1.4, moved by M. Janz, carried 6-0: three minutes per approved speaker for the whole meeting.
Approved on the bike-lane item: 64 entries (15 under an organization's name); whole meeting: 79.
Recorded as presenting on the bike-lane item: 52 entries (12 under an organization's name). This is below the 60-80 band, so the finding is definition-sensitive.
No City record states why the motion was moved.
